title: Cultural Differences in Web Design on Chinese and Western Websites
notes: Findings taken from docs/01 section 2.1. The authors note that definitions and methods are not uniform across the reviewed studies.

title: Cross-Cultural Design: Comparing the Visual Characteristics of Chinese and Western Municipal Websites
sample: 100 Chinese and 100 Western municipal homepages (institutional sites, not commercial apps)
notes: Figures taken from docs/01 section 2.2. Shows differences in this sample, not universal user preferences.

title: Are Chinese Websites Too Complex?
sample: Think-aloud usability testing with 12 participants (6 native Chinese users, 6 expatriates living in China), 2 tasks each on 8 of 14 Chinese sites; small, qualitative
notes: Primary text read on 2026-11-09 (nngroup.com). It reports that Chinese participants tolerate and prefer fairly high information density, especially on portal and news sites, but also hit many usability problems on complex sites and found some too complicated. It does NOT report a general Western preference for simplicity: its foreign participants were expatriates in China, who were less annoyed by problems on simple sites than on complex ones.

title: Project synthesis of Western vs Chinese interface composition
sample: Narrative synthesis (docs/01 sections 3-6, docs/02), not independent data
notes: Own synthesis of the cited studies and observed platforms. Cannot raise an evidence level on its own.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sample: Accessibility standard (success criteria 1.4.1 use of colour, 1.4.3 contrast minimum, 1.4.12 text spacing, 2.5.8 target size)
notes: Used only as a constraint on effects, never as evidence of cultural difference. Criteria cited from general knowledge; text not re-read in this project.
